If I be wak'd, see thou be stirring too; Then come a Gib as big as Ascapart VVe'l make him play at Leap-frog. A brave Souldiers lodging, The floore my Bed, a Milstone for my Pillow, The Sayles for Curtaynes. So good night.
speeches.Rob: Be patient I beseech you, what doe you meane Sir?
speeches.Arth,: You tell me wonders. Since all your words to me are Oracles, And such as I most constantly beleeve. But Sir, shall I be bold and plaine withall, I am suspitious all's not well at home; I dare proceed no farther without leave, Yet there is something lodged within my breast Which I am loath to utter.
speeches.Bant: No, but I am afflicted to thinke that the divell should have power to put such a trick upon us, to countenance a Rascal, that is one.
No reliefe. Come my sweet Puckling.
No comfort! My Mamilion. Mamilion, ho Mamilion, Mamilion. My friend, my Sweet-heart, my Mamilion. 'Tis folly to dissemble yie sir, I am one. Yes Sir. A matter of sixe yeares Sir. Yes when I pleas'd. Tis folly to dissemble; twice a Weeke he never fail'd me. Tis folly to speake worse of him than he is. He pleas'd me well Sir, like a proper man. Onely his flesh felt cold. Gentleman like, but blacke blacke points and all.
